title: Introduce rate-shear safeguard and tenant evacuation protocol with circuit buffering
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Added a rate-shear safeguard that smooths incoming spike profiles and a tenant evacuation protocol with circuit buffering to reduce KV cache churn. New telemetry and alerts for RateShear.Exceeded and Evacuation.OPT_OUT to help SREs. Backwards compatible runtime flags; opt-in via cluster config.
description: Summary: This PR implements a rate-shear safeguard and a coordinated tenant evacuation protocol to reduce noisy evictions and mass KV cache invalidations during regional or node pressure events. The primary goal is to stop short, high-amplitude bursts from tripping downstream circuits and to give the serving runtime a deterministic path to evacuate tenants with minimal cold-start penalty. Motivation: During a February incident we observed sudden traffic spikes from a small cohort of tenants that caused widespread KV cache evaporation and thundering retries when regional failover kicked in. Existing load-shedding used coarse circuit breakers which caused worse tail latency for unaffected tenants. This change introduces two complementary pieces: 1) RateShear Safeguard: a transient shaping layer that detects high-frequency burst profiles (short-window derivative) and applies an adaptive micro-smoothing policy per-tenant or per-route. The policy uses exponential backoff on effective admission rate with a short decay window so normal traffic ramps back quickly. 2) Tenant Evacuation Protocol with Circuit Buffering: an orderly evacuation handshake that marks tenants for evacuation, drains in-flight connections, snapshots KV-affinity tags and a small serialized cache delta (bounded by size), and transitions the tenant through a buffered-circuit state to avoid immediate full-eviction. This buffering gives downstream nodes a short grace period to accept warmed KV deltas and prevents simultaneous cold cache rebuilding. What changed (high-level commits): - introduce RateShear detector and micro-smoother in serving/runtime/ingress (detector + policy + unit tests) - add evacuation coordinator in controlplane/evac and evacuation API hooks for private deployments - implement circuit buffer state, small on-disk serialized delta format, and KV snapshot exporter - add telemetry: RateShear.Exceeded, Evacuation.Start/Finish/Abort, CircuitBuffer.Hit/Miss - add canary config and runtime flags to enable gradual rollout - integration tests for regional failover + eviction protection - docs/operational playbook entry and runbook updates Key files touched (representative): - serving/runtime/ingress/rate_shear.go (+ tests) - serving/runtime/ingress/smoother_policy.go - controlplane/evac/coordinator.go - serving/runtime/circuit/buffer.go - internal/kv/snapshot_exporter.go - telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml - docs/ops/evacuation-playbook.md - tests/integration/evacuation_integration_test.go - examples/cli/evacate-tenant.sh Detailed notes (single-line paragraphs to preserve continuity): Design: RateShear detector computes a short-window rate derivative and classifies traffic as steady, ramp, or shear. For shear profiles we apply a per-tenant token-bucket scaled down by an adaptive factor computed from recent shear magnitude and cluster headroom. The micro-smoother is intentionally conservative to avoid harming steady low-latency flows. Evacuation protocol is a 3-phase flow: mark->drain->snapshot->buffer->handoff. The buffer holds serialized KV deltas and a soft TTL to allow downstream fetchers to warm without triggering full rehydration. Telemetry & alerts: new metrics are added and wired into the SLO dashboard; added an alert that fires when RateShear.Exceeded > 5/min across cluster and sustained for 2 minutes. This alert is informational at first (pager opt-in) and will be promoted if we see false negatives. Backwards compatibility: feature gates everywhere, cluster-config knob to enable per-tenant experiments, private installer includes new flag for on-prem KMS export path. Rollout plan: 1) Enable RateShear detection (no smoothing) in canary region for 24h and monitor false positives. 2) Turn on micro-smoother for 10% of tenants with low risk tags. 3) Enable evacuation protocol in canary with conservative buffer size (2MB per tenant) for 48h. 4) Gradually increase coverage and reduce buffer TTL after observing warm-hit rates. Tests: unit tests for detection thresholds and smoother hysteresis added; integration harness simulates bursty traffic and verifies max tail latency does not increase by >5% while eviction rates drop by >30%. CI: full test matrix passed on linux/amd and arm build nodes; flaky test (integration/evacuation_integration_test) was rerun once and passed. Review discussion (highlights): - Ethan: asked for clarification on worst-case memory usage for buffers. Response: buffer is size-bounded per-tenant and uses spill-to-disk with LRU eviction; added memory guard in buffer.go and documented behavior. - Priya: requested clearer metrics for 'evac snapshot success rate'. Response: added Evacuation.SnapshotSuccess and added percentile timing metrics. - Maya: safety concern around cross-region handoff race. Response: added a short randomized jitter on handoff and strengthened idempotency checks. - SRE review (Maya): asked for playbook; author added docs/ops/evacuation-playbook.md with steps and rollback commands. Performance: microbenchmarks show <1% throughput regression at 99th percentile under steady load, and a 40% reduction in tenant-driven cold-start events in synthetic burst tests. Observability: dashboards added for RateShear, BufferHitRate, EvacSnapshotLatency, and EvacAbortReasons. Operators can tune thresholds via console under 'Serving -> RateShear' and 'ControlPlane -> Evacuation'. Migration/installer notes: private-installer has an optional step to provision a buffer storage path and set KMS access; failing to provide it disables snapshot export and falls back to immediate evacuation (documented in release notes). Security/Privacy: snapshots are bounded and encrypted with KMS before being written to buffer storage; added a data retention policy defaulting to 1 hour. Risk assessment: small risk of false-positive smoothing on bursty legitimate traffic; mitigated by gradual rollout, telemetry, and operator knobs. Release notes (summary): introduced RateShear safeguard and Tenant Evacuation Protocol with circuit buffering to reduce cascade evictions and KV cold-start churn. Rollout behind feature flag. No breaking changes. Merge: merged via squash with commit message "runtime: add rate shear smoothing and evac protocol (ENG-2487)". Changelog entry authored. Follow-ups: - ENG-2488: automatic threshold tuning via ML-informed headroom model - SRE-333: emergency runbook optimization and alert thresholds tuning - DEVEX-101: add TS/Python SDK flag helpers for evict API Usage examples and small snippets added to docs. Contact: reach out to author (sofia@redwood.ai) or reviewers for troubleshooting.
